git_basics.notes: Advanced to proficient after mastering remote workflows. Complete understanding of local vs remote operations (git remote, git push, git pull, git clone, git fetch). Demonstrates professional-level remote repository management with upstream tracking and multi-device synchronization. Ready for advanced Git workflows (branching strategies, merge conflicts, rebasing).

terminal_comfort.notes: Advanced to competent. Fluent with core commands (ls, cd, mkdir, echo, touch) and Git operations. Demonstrates understanding of file paths, directory navigation, and command-line workflows. Ready for more complex terminal operations (pipes, redirects, process management).

markdown_documentation.notes: Created comprehensive README.md with proper markdown formatting (headers, lists, code blocks). Documented project vision, features, tech stack professionally. Portfolio-ready documentation skills.

project_organization.notes: Proactively created .gitignore for Python/Node artifacts. Understands importance of repository cleanliness. Ready for more complex project structures (src/ directories, config files, documentation folders).

technical_vocabulary.notes: Advanced to competent. Expanded vocabulary: remote repository, origin, upstream, SSH key, Personal Access Token, ssh-agent, git fetch, git pull, git clone, git push. Strong command of Git-specific terminology and authentication concepts. Demonstrates ability to explain technical concepts clearly.

systems_thinking.notes: Strong understanding of local vs remote architecture. Recognized multi-device sync patterns and workflow discipline (pull-before-work). Identified vulnerability of unpushed commits (Lake Berryessa scenario). Shows architectural awareness and risk assessment thinking.

commit_message_writing.notes: Professional-grade commit messages following Conventional Commits format (feat, docs, chore types). Uses imperative mood, keeps messages concise (<50 chars), provides clear scope. Portfolio-ready commit history.

github_workflow.notes: NEW SKILL. Demonstrates professional GitHub workflow understanding: remote connection (git remote add), pushing with upstream tracking (git push -u), cloning repositories, multi-device synchronization (pull → work → commit → push). Understands disaster recovery, portfolio building, and collaboration benefits. Ready for GitHub collaboration features (pull requests, issues, code review).

ssh_authentication.notes: NEW SKILL. Already had SSH configured from previous work (The Odin Project, dev-curriculum). Excellent understanding of ssh-agent purpose, SSH vs HTTPS tradeoffs, and Personal Access Token distinctions. Professional-level authentication setup. Ready for advanced scenarios (multiple SSH keys, SSH config management).

remote_repository_management.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete understanding of remote operations: git remote add, git push -u (upstream tracking), git fetch vs git pull, git clone. Demonstrates multi-device workflow discipline and divergent history prevention. Ready for advanced remote scenarios (multiple remotes, force push, remote branch management).

multi_device_sync.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent visualization of two-computer workflow (pull → work → commit → push → repeat). Understands importance of pulling before starting work to avoid conflicts. Ready for real-world multi-device CatchBook development scenarios.
